Good pushback, and it exposes a mistake in my earlier reasoning. Let me correct it properly.

## The correction

I said earlier that removing §2.2's row alone would "strip the warning while the risk remains." That's wrong, or at least overstated, I hadn't re-checked whether the same warning exists anywhere else. It does, in three places, independently of §2.2:

- **Appendix C's own section header**, right above the Sprint-2 table itself: *"Sprint 2 content types (provisional, field sets inferred, not confirmed; pending authoring review)"*, arguably the best-placed version of this warning, since it sits directly next to the actual content it's warning about.
- **§7's risk row**: *"Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred, not confirmed... keep provisional."*
- **§8's Decision Record**: *"Sprint-2 content types provisional pending an authoring review with Emma and Dani."*

So the warning doesn't disappear if §2.2's row goes, it survives in three other places, one of which is more directly useful than §2.2's version anyway.

## What actually changes if we remove §2.2's row and nothing else

- **§2.2 shrinks from 4 assumption rows to 3.** A reader scanning only §2.2 would no longer see this one listed there specifically, but that's a narrower loss than "the warning disappears from the document."
- **No DoD conflict.** Appendix C's own header still carries the "provisional, not confirmed" flag right next to the actual content, so "content model requirements... accurately captured, including their confirmed/provisional status" stays true.
- **No destination needed.** Nothing is being extracted or pointed anywhere, we're just removing one of four redundant statements of the same fact.
- **A small, real step against the actual drift concern.** The same fact was stated four times before this; cutting it to three is itself a small reduction in exactly the kind of duplication Tim is worried about.
- **§2.2 still functions structurally.** The template's definition of an Assumptions section (things treated as true, with a Risk-if-Wrong column) doesn't require this specific row, the remaining three (SSR-first not built, connector-app behavior, US-International) still do that job fine.

## Verdict

Given this, removing §2.2's row on its own is actually fine, clean even. It closes comment #3 literally, doesn't lose the warning, doesn't touch Appendix C, and doesn't create any DoD gap. I was wrong to call it a regression earlier. Want me to draft the removal plus the updated reply for that thread now?

name: sfcc-249-reformat-draft
description: "SFCC-249 Contentful TSD reformatted into the prescribed template — PUBLISHED to Confluence page 346783750 as v31 (replaced v30 in place, 01 Aug 2026); pending BA-Lead + SA sign-off. Local mirror on Marcel's Desktop"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 01fb0dfa-fa41-471c-88f9-4d3bc8b4a857
  modified: 2026-07-31T22:50:00.545Z
---

The Contentful Integration TSD (source Confluence **346783750 v30**) was restructured into the prescribed 8-section TSD template (Confluence **352419841**) and **PUBLISHED to Confluence page 346783750 as v31** on 01 Aug 2026 (updated in place, replacing v30; v30 retained in the page's Confluence version history; page title kept as "Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model (SFCC-249)"). Local mirror at `~/Desktop/SFCC-249-contentful-integration-tsd-REFORMAT-DRAFT.md`. Approach = best-fit "Option 2": template spine §1-8 clean, ticket-required breadth in Appendices A/B/C.

**Scope guardrails held (per Marcel's explicit boundary):** no PWA TSD §12.1 edit (linked, not restated); no Jira cards raised; owner-pending items captured in §7, not resolved. Only in-lane decisions made: the counts and the Studio-vs-coded rule.

**Substantive changes beyond a reformat (all validated against source):** corrected the preview-token boundary to the decided **client-side Live Preview** design (per PR #41/#43 + `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`); reconciled locale/storefront counts; scoped the SFCC-ID pattern as the single **Option A** (page-scoping) and routed reference-resolution to **SFCC-238**; established the **Studio Experiences vs coded-component** authoring rule (§5.5); flagged doc inconsistencies (CMA-token; CPA server-vs-client) in §7.

**Key verified facts baked in (2 recursive V&V rounds, 4 audit agents + mechanical passes):**
- **Counts:** 8 storefronts = 8 SFCC sites at target (1:1); **7 SFCC sites wired today**, US-International pending as a **separate** site `ZimmermannUSIntl` (currently a filtered-out stub in `countries.ts`, no locale assigned — may add a 10th Contentful locale when wired). EU-domestic's one SFCC site serves 4 language routes, so routes(11) > sites(8). **9 Contentful locales** (`en,en-US,en-GB,fr,it,es,en-CH,en-HK,en-AE`); 11 storefront-locale routes (10 wired). PWA TSD 256835585 + Product TSD 292061208 already count 8 SFCC sites. (Round-1 wrongly claimed US-dom+intl share one site → 7; round-2 corrected it. See [[sfcc-123]].)
- **Code state:** SFCC-ID fields (`sfccCategoryId`/`sfccProductId`) NOT in code (proposed). `useContentful.ts` = client-side REST `include=2`; SSR-first/GraphQL/webhook receiver NOT built. SDK `contentful@11.12.4` axios-based (`CreateClientParams` has httpsAgent/httpAgent/adapter, NO dispatcher). `connectionPools.ts` = 7 undici pools, defined-but-unwired, no Contentful pool. CPA token client-side per PR #43 (OPEN, base `develop`); PR #41 CLOSED (Marcel raised CPA, mani060689 ruled "intentional by design"). Both #3 spikes (PLP pagination; PDP accordion mixed-content) genuinely UNCARDED.

**Credit:** Marcel Angelo Navarro = reformat author + technical review + validation + open-item triage; Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz = original spike draft (SFCC-123). Version History itemises the substantive work ("technical review and restructure, not only a reformat"). Sign-off = **Jasmijn Tsang (BA Lead) + Tim Lavelle (SA)**, both Pending. Document Information = exactly the template's 7 fields (no Contributors row).

**Status (01 Aug 2026): PUBLISHED as page 346783750 v31.** V&V-converged (2 recursive rounds); template-conformant (only deviation = the intentional Appendices breadth). Page content Status = "Draft - for review, not approved for implementation"; sign-off (Jasmijn Tsang BA Lead + Tim Lavelle SA) still **Pending**. SFCC-249 is in **Code Review**; its DoD = review + feedback + BA-Lead/SA sign-off (reformatting itself was not a ticket requirement). **Caveats from publishing in place:** (a) updating the body may have marked some of Jhoan's inline comments on the page as "outdated" (their anchored text changed); (b) the planned one-line heads-up to Tim on the shape was NOT sent first — Marcel published directly. Next: BA-Lead + SA review/sign-off; the §7 open items remain owner-pending (not ours to close).

**Process files (not loaded at session start):** `~/.claude/plans/if-we-execute-the-compressed-honey.md` (reformat plan + full 16-item concern triage with dispositions) and `~/.claude/plans/this-decision-log-is-parsed-dusk.md` (trimmed 5-decision record + execution notes).

Related: [[sfcc-123]], [[sfcc-123-review-marcel-actions]], [[tsd-scope-principle]].

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

**Reply to comment #3 (§2.2, Sprint-2 field-sets assumption row)**

The same "Sprint-2 fields inferred, not confirmed" warning is already stated independently in three other places: Appendix C's own Sprint-2 section header, the §7 risk table, and the §8 Decision Record. Removing it from §2.2 doesn't lose the warning, it just cuts one of four repeated statements of the same fact. **Reply to comment #11 (§5.2, sfccCategoryId/sfccProductId field-definition row)**

**Reply to comment #12 (§5.2, one-component-per-content-type row)**

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. 1. Problem Statement
--------------------

### 1.1 Context

Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards.

### 1.2 Problem

Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards.

### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved

Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build.

### 1.4 Success Criteria

1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue.
2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories.
3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined.
4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners.
5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy.

*These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.*

3. Options Analysis
-------------------

> The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document.

### 3.1 Options Summary

| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync). + SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash). + Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. + The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages. - All SFCC-ID filtering happens once, in the MRT SSR layer; components hold none of their own. A bug there affects every page of that content type at once, with no fallback to catch it. | Yes (recommended) |
| **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift). - Couples the two systems. - Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected |
| **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash). - Ships unneeded entries to the browser. - Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No |

### 3.2 Option Detail

#### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5.

#### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected)

Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume.

#### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)*

Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components.

4. Recommended Option & Rationale
---------------------------------

### 4.1 Recommended Option

**Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.**

### 4.2 Rationale

Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B introduces and requires a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238.

### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted

* Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages.
* This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5).

5. Technical Implementation
---------------------------

### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow)

1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X).
2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA).
3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type.
4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component.
5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output).
6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated).
7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys.

> **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live.

### 5.2 Component / API Changes

| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified |
| `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New |
| GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New |

> Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**.

### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces

**Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields):

| Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. |
| `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. |
| `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

**Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert):

`{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: [],
}`

**MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):**

`const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({
content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',
locale: currentLocale,
});
const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => {
const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;
// null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render
return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId;
});
// Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component
return matchedInserts;`

**Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.

**Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages.

### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error |
| Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case |
| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error |
| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case |
| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error |
| Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case |
| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case |

> **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Note that Contentful is browser-direct today, so there is no MRT-side Contentful connection pool to isolate; this becomes relevant only if the SSR-first fetch is adopted. The `contentful` v11 SDK is axios-based and exposes `httpsAgent`/`httpAgent`/`adapter` (not undici's `dispatcher`); see the correction tracked against 12.1 in Section 7.

### 5.5 Configuration & Environment Notes

**Environments and locales.** A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially; production resolves via an alias. **9 Contentful locales** (`en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`) serve the **8 storefronts** (`en-GB` is shared by the UK and EU-domestic-English routes). Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7.

**Token boundary.**

| Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI service account, and each developer's own local `.env` | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Personal per-developer tokens for local work; a separate CI service-account token for automation. Never in MRT or the browser bundle. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). |

**Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:

* **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.
* **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide.
* **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.
* Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.

This spike produces findings and a design, not a testable build; the tests below belong to the downstream build stories.

| Test Type | What is Being Tested | Pass Criteria |

| Validation of findings (this spike) | The design cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence (maps to Section 1.4). | Every design claim traces to a verified source; current-versus-target state is stated honestly. |
| Unit (downstream) | SSR-side SFCC-ID filter; presentation-only component renders pre-filtered entries and null-returns on empty. | Filter selects matching + null-ID entries only; component holds no ID logic. |
| Integration (downstream) | SSR cache key includes the SFCC ID; publish webhook purges the correct keys. | No cross-page editorial bleed; content updates appear after publish within the SWR window. |
| E2E / Playwright (downstream) | Editorial content renders on the scoped category/product page and not elsewhere. | Observable in the UI across representative storefronts. |

### 6.2 Regression Risk

Low today: the reformatted design does not change running code. The material regression surface arrives with the downstream build, concentrated on two points that the build stories must cover explicitly: **SSR ID-filter correctness** and **cache-key isolation** (a wrong or missing key leaks editorial content across pages).

## Overall state of the TSD

Mechanically clean. All 3 rows are gone, no broken tables, no dangling cross-references pointing at the deleted text, and every fact those rows stated is still findable elsewhere in the document (§5.3, §5.5, Appendix C, §7, §8). The document still satisfies its own Success Criteria (§1.4) and the governing tickets' Definition of Done, content model, field definitions, and authoring rules are all still captured, just not duplicated across as many locations.

Of Tim's original review comments, most of the substantive ones are now actioned: 10th-locale, SSR cache-keys/centralized-filtering, connector-app validation, and now these 3 drift-risk rows. What's left open: the §5.5 authoring-path/heuristic dispute (#13/#14, untouched), Tim's broader "component requirement pages" suggestion (no decision made, SFCC-323 unevaluated), Appendix A `[FOR UPDATE]`, and both sign-offs still Pending. None of that is new, it predates this pass.

## Implications of the removal

The three rows don't have the same profile, worth being precise about which risk was actually resolved versus reduced:

- **§5.2 field-definition row and one-component row**: each had exactly one duplicate (§5.3 and §5.5 respectively). Removing them fully collapses each fact to a single source. Clean resolution.
- **§2.2 Sprint-2 row**: had three other copies (Appendix C header, §7, §8). Removing it takes the count from four to three, it reduces the drift surface, it doesn't eliminate it. The remaining three could still independently drift from each other and from Appendix C's actual table.
- A softer, genre-level implication for §2.2 specifically: an Assumptions section (§2.2) and a Risks section (§7) serve different rhetorical jobs, an assumption is a premise the document's own argument leans on; a risk is a project-level open item to track before build. Sprint-2 field uncertainty was arguably both. It now only lives as a Risk (§7) and as descriptive context (Appendix C), not as a stated premise of the design itself. Minor, and Tim's own framing ("drift risk") supports the removal, but worth naming since you asked specifically about implications.
- Ownership attribution (Emma and Dani, Tim) survived the removal intact, it's still named in §7 and §8. Nothing was lost there.

## Gaps, holes, or discrepancies introduced

Two real ones, one already flagged and one new on reflection:

1. **§5.2 no longer states a build task for the SFCC-ID fields.** Before, §5.2 was the section that said, in effect, "add these fields to these content types." Now that instruction doesn't exist anywhere as an actionable line, §5.3 only shows the fields descriptively, and Appendix B's checklist item ("author all Sprint 1/2 content-type definitions + components") is too generic to stand in for it. Someone using §5.2 as their punch list would miss this specific task. 2. **The 3 comment threads are now orphaned in Confluence**, since the text they were anchored to no longer exists, they'll drop to the page's general comment list rather than sit inline. No table corruption, no broken section cross-references, and no contradiction between the three remaining copies of the Sprint-2 caveat (Appendix C, §7, §8 all say the same thing, just phrased differently). The removals were surgical, the two gaps above are the only things worth acting on.

"Studio Experience" components: whole author-composed pages, registered via `defineComponents` in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts`, rendered through Contentful's visual Experience Builder, served via a `/:slug` route. Currently 3 are registered: collectionHero, imageText, shoppableImage.
2. "Coded content-type components": fixed slots in dev-built commerce templates (homepage modules, PLP inserts, PDP tabs, footer, nav, banner) that consume a Contentful CDA content type via the `useContentful` hook, where the author only edits field values, not placement.

A Solution Architect pushed back on this doc's proposed authoring-path rule, arguing (paraphrased in a Confluence comment): "I'm not sure we need to separate these, the components we build will most of the time being used in an experience builder." I need to find out whether the actual codebase gives real evidence for or against that claim. Specifically, please investigate and report back with concrete file paths/line numbers as evidence:

1. List everything currently registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` (Studio Experience components) verbatim, and what each one's underlying component implementation looks like (is it a thin wrapper, or does it duplicate logic also used elsewhere?).
2. List everything under `overrides/app/components/contentful/` that is NOT in the experiences folder (the "coded content-type" components), and check whether ANY of those same components are also referenced/imported by anything under the experiences folder or by an Experience-Builder-related code path. I'm looking for concrete evidence of dual-path usage (a single component used both as a fixed dev-placed slot AND inside an author-composed Experience Builder page), which would support the SA's pushback, versus evidence that the two sets are cleanly disjoint, which would support keeping the rule.
3. Specifically check `shoppableImage`: it's flagged in the design doc as "straddles both authoring paths, owner call needed." Find its actual implementation(s) and confirm whether it exists as ONE component used both ways, or as two separate implementations (one Studio-registered, one coded).
4. Check git log / git blame on `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and the coded content-type component directory for how recently these were added/changed, and whether there's a commit message or PR that explains the intended split (or lack thereof).
5. Check `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` and anything importing it, to see if it's used inside experience-builder-rendered pages too, or strictly outside them.
6. Search the repo's `.docs/` folder for anything describing the Studio Experience vs coded component distinction, an authoring model, or Experience Builder usage guidance, to see if there's already documented intent beyond the TSD in question.

Report back factually with file:line citations for every claim. Do not speculate beyond what the code/docs/git history actually show. If something is ambiguous or you can't find clear evidence either way, say so explicitly rather than guessing. Keep the report well-organized by the 6 points above, and end with a one-paragraph summary of whether the codebase evidence leans toward "keep the two paths separate" or "don't bother separating them, most things end up in the experience builder anyway," or is inconclusive.

## 1. What's registered in `experiences/definitions.ts`

`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` is an **autogenerated** file (line 1: `// AUTOGENERATED — do not edit. Source: ./*.tsx`) produced by `scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs` from `@cf-register`/`@cf` JSDoc tags on files in the `experiences/` folder (confirmed by `scripts/contentful/README.md:19-52` and `.claude/skills/contentful-register-component/SKILL.md`). It registers exactly 3 components via `defineComponents([...])`, matching the doc's premise:

| id | component | variables |
|---|---|---|
| `collection-hero` (definitions.ts:12) | `CollectionHero` | headline, subheadline, ctaLabel, ctaUrl, backgroundImage — all `Text`/`Media` |
| `image-text` (definitions.ts:26) | `ImageText` | image, imageAlt, headline, body, imagePosition |
| `shoppable-image` (definitions.ts:40) | `ShoppableImage` | image, imageAlt, hotspots (`Text`, i.e. JSON-as-string) |

Implementation shape of each:

- **`CollectionHero`** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/collectionHero.tsx:1-49`) — a thin, self-contained Chakra layout wrapper. No imports of, or logic shared with, anything outside `experiences/`. No `ContentfulLivePreview` usage.
- **`ImageText`** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/imageText.tsx:1-46`) — likewise a thin, self-contained Chakra layout wrapper, no external logic reuse, no `ContentfulLivePreview` usage.
- **`ShoppableImage`** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/shoppableImage.tsx:1-66`) — not a thin wrapper. It imports `HotspotMarker` (`.../experiences/hotspotMarker.tsx`), which itself imports `HotspotPopup` (`.../experiences/hotspotPopup.tsx`). `HotspotPopup` calls `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (hotspotPopup.tsx:3,12) and `proxyImageUrl` from `overrides/app/utils/sfccImage.ts` (hotspotPopup.tsx:5) — the **same utility function also imported by the coded `ProductHero` component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx:5,38`). `ShoppableImage` itself also imports and calls `ContentfulLivePreview.getProps` (shoppableImage.tsx:3, 51) with an `entryId`/`locale` prop pair — a pattern otherwise used only by the four coded components (see §5).

## 2. Everything under `contentful/` outside `experiences/`, and cross-references

Files (not in `experiences/`):
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/heroBanner.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/duplexSection.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/videoEmbed.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts` (barrel)

All four coded components were added in the same initial commit as everything else (`cd60b7a`, 2026-06-12) and are consumed **exactly once**, from `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:20` (`import { HeroBanner, DuplexSection, VideoEmbed, ProductHero } from '../../components/contentful'`), rendered in `HomepageContent` (home/index.tsx:64-80) driven by a Contentful `homepage` content type fetched via `useContentfulEntries`/`useContentfulEntry` (home/index.tsx:24, 148, 175).

Cross-reference check, both directions:
- **Coded → experiences**: none of `heroBanner.tsx`, `duplexSection.tsx`, `videoEmbed.tsx`, `productHero.tsx` import anything from `experiences/` — a repo-wide grep for `heroBanner|HeroBanner|duplexSection|...` inside `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` returns no hits. These four are cleanly disjoint from the Experience Builder path.
- **Experiences → coded / barrel**: `overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts:5` does `export { default as ShoppableImage } from './experiences/shoppableImage';` — i.e., the barrel file that's supposed to hold "coded content-type" exports also re-exports the Experience-registered `ShoppableImage`. **However**, nothing in the codebase actually imports `ShoppableImage` through that barrel — a repo-wide grep for `components/contentful'` imports (outside the `contentful/` folder itself) finds only `home/index.tsx:20`, which imports `HeroBanner, DuplexSection, VideoEmbed, ProductHero` — **not** `ShoppableImage`. So this is a dangling/unused dual-export, not an active dual-consumption.

There is currently no PLP-insert, PDP-tab, footer, nav, or banner component under `overrides/app/components/contentful/` at all — a grep for `contentful|Contentful` across `overrides/app/pages` and `overrides/app/components` (excluding the `contentful/` folder itself) returns only `_app-config/index.tsx` (the `ContentfulLivePreviewProvider` wrapper), `pages/experience/index.tsx`, and `pages/home/index.tsx`. The "PLP inserts / PDP tabs / footer / nav / banner" coded slots described in the design doc are **not yet implemented** — they exist only as open items in `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:31-33` and PRD entries (`.docs/prd/plp.md:22-23` "Inline Editorial Hero SPR-64", `.docs/prd/pdp.md:152-153` "Seen on the Runway PRD-023"). So for those specific surfaces, the codebase gives **no evidence either way** yet — the only real, running example of both patterns today is Home (coded) vs. Experience (`/:slug`) pages.

## 3. `shoppableImage` — one component or two?

There is **one** React implementation: `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/shoppableImage.tsx`. It is not duplicated as a separate coded component file. But it is registered/typed for **both** paths simultaneously, and the evidence shows the two registrations don't cleanly agree:

- **Experience Builder registration**: `definitions.ts:37-48`, id `shoppable-image`, variable `hotspots: { type: 'Text', ... }` — i.e. Experience Builder authors enter hotspots as a raw JSON **string**. `shoppableImage.tsx:18-35` (`parseHotspots`) accordingly expects `hotspots?: string` and does `JSON.parse(raw)`.
- **Standalone content-type registration**: `scripts/contentful/content-types/shoppableImage.js:1-37` defines a live Contentful content type `shoppableImage` with `hotspots` as field type `'Object'` (line 28-35), and `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:62-77` (`ShoppableImageEntry`) types `fields.hotspots` as `Hotspot[]` — an **already-parsed array**, not a string. `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:53-55` (`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS.shoppableImage`) and its comment at line 63 ("Matches the shape expected by .../experiences/shoppableImage") reference this same component.
- **Consequence**: if a coded page ever fetched a `shoppableImage` entry via `useContentfulEntries<ShoppableImageEntry>('shoppableImage')` (the hook at `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` does no extra parsing of `Object`-type fields — it only resolves `Asset` links, see `useContentful.ts:113-127`) and passed `fields.hotspots` straight into the existing `ShoppableImage` component, `parseHotspots` would receive an array, not a string, `JSON.parse([...])` would throw, and the `catch` (shoppableImage.tsx:32-34) would silently swallow all hotspots. The two registrations are not prop-compatible as they stand.
- **Live-preview wiring mismatch**: `shoppableImage.tsx:50-51` accepts `entryId?: string; locale?: string` and calls `ContentfulLivePreview.getProps({ entryId, fieldId: 'image', locale })` — identical to the pattern used by the four coded components (`heroBanner.tsx:20`, `duplexSection.tsx:61`, `videoEmbed.tsx:20`, `productHero.tsx:14`). But when rendered through Experience Builder, the SDK does not supply `entryId`/`locale` to registered components — per `node_modules/@contentful/experiences-sdk-react/dist/src/utils/withComponentWrapper.d.ts`, wrapped components instead receive `data-cf-node-id` / `data-cf-node-block-id` / `data-cf-node-block-type` props. Neither of the two purely Experience-only components (`CollectionHero`, `ImageText`) accepts or uses `entryId`/`locale`/`ContentfulLivePreview` at all. So `ShoppableImage`'s `entryId`/`locale`/live-preview code is dead weight in its one currently-active registration path (Experience Builder) and only makes sense for the coded path it isn't actually wired into.
- Corroborating project memory: `.docs/memory/projectState.md:42` explicitly logs this as **"ShoppableImage component — Experience Builder component + standard content type"** with the content type "synced to Contentful (mock space) 2026-05-11" — i.e. the dual-registration is a known, deliberate (if unfinished) design, not an accident, but it has not been fully realized/tested for the coded side.

**Conclusion for item 3**: it is one implementation, deliberately scaffolded for both paths (registered in `definitions.ts` for Experience Builder, and separately schema-synced as a CDA content type), but currently only actually *consumed* through the Experience Builder path in running code, and its two registrations disagree on the `hotspots` prop shape — a concrete "owner call needed" situation, exactly as the design doc flags.

## 4. Git history

```
overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts:
  5aafaae 2026-07-13  fix(contentful): address CodeRabbit findings on codegen and docs
  d5012bc 2026-07-03  feat(contentful): Added Contentful Studio/Experiences definition codegen/automation
  cd60b7a 2026-06-12  Initial commit during Detailed Design phase

overrides/app/components/contentful/{heroBanner,duplexSection,videoEmbed,productHero}.tsx, index.ts:
  cd60b7a 2026-06-12  Initial commit during Detailed Design phase   (only commit for all five)

overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/shoppableImage.tsx:
  03524b5 2026-07-13, d5012bc 2026-07-03, cd60b7a 2026-06-12

scripts/contentful/content-types/shoppableImage.js:
  cd60b7a 2026-06-12  Initial commit during Detailed Design phase   (only commit; created same commit as shoppableImage.tsx)
```

All coded components and all three Experience components (plus the `shoppableImage.js` content-type schema) were introduced in the **same single initial commit** (`cd60b7a`, "Initial commit during Detailed Design phase") — there was no later, distinct commit where the project "decided" to split the two paths; both existed side by side from day one. `git show cd60b7a -s --format=fuller` shows no body text beyond the one-line subject, so no rationale is recorded there.

The two subsequent substantive commits (`d5012bc` "Added Contentful Studio/Experiences definition codegen/automation", `5aafaae` "fix(contentful): address CodeRabbit findings on codegen and docs") are about **tooling** (the `@cf`-tag → `definitions.ts` codegen pipeline) — not about the architectural split itself. The actual documented rationale for keeping the two paths distinct lives in project docs, not commit messages:
- `scripts/contentful/README.md:64-68` — section literally titled **"Don't cross the streams"**: *"A Studio Experiences component (`experiences/*.tsx`) does not belong in content-types/ — sync.js does not understand it. A content-type definition (content-types/*.js) does not belong in experiences/ — it is an API artefact, not a runtime component."*
- `.docs/architecture.md:187` — *"Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in .../experiences/definitions.ts and do not need a corresponding sync:contentful entry **unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio**."* (this is the explicit escape hatch that `shoppableImage` exercises)
- `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md:87-99` — `scripts/contentful/content-types/` is governed under a distinct "Owner: Integration / SI Partner" protection rule, separate from the (unprotected, autogenerated) `experiences/definitions.ts` — a further sign the two paths are intended to have different ownership/process, not just different code location.

## 5. `useContentful.ts` usage

`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` exports `useContentfulEntry` and `useContentfulEntries` (both plain CDA/CPA `fetch`-based hooks, lines 26-89 and 91-157). A repo-wide grep for importers of `useContentful` returns exactly one file: **`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`** (lines 24, 148, 175) — used in `HomeNormal` (`useContentfulEntries<HomepageEntry>('homepage')`, line 148) and `HomePreviewContent` (`useContentfulEntry<AnyContentfulEntry>(entryId, true)`, line 175).

It is **never** imported by `pages/experience/index.tsx` or by anything under `experiences/`. The Experience-Builder-rendered page instead uses the Contentful `contentful` JS SDK's `createClient` plus `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react`'s `useFetchBySlug`/`ExperienceRoot` (`pages/experience/index.tsx:4-5, 45-68`) — a completely separate data-fetching path from `useContentful.ts`. So today, `useContentful.ts` is used strictly outside the Experience-Builder-rendered page, confirming a clean split at the **data-fetching** layer, even though (per §3) the `ShoppableImage` component itself was coded with both consumption patterns in mind.

## 6. `.docs/` documentation of the authoring-model distinction

Documentation already describing this split (beyond the TSD in dispute) exists in several places:

- `scripts/contentful/README.md` — full write-up of "two different Contentful surfaces" (content types vs. Studio Experiences component definitions), ending in the explicit "Don't cross the streams" rule (lines 64-68, quoted above).
- `.docs/architecture.md:160-187` — "Contentful Content Type Management" section, culminating in the line noting Experience Builder components are "a separate concern," with the explicit caveat that a component *can* have both when "they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio" (line 187) — i.e., the doc anticipates and permits the exact `shoppableImage` situation.
- `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md:294` (§7.3, "Contentful schema as code") — *"Each definition pairs with a typed React component... Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module."* This is the current TSD's own architecture section stating the split as settled fact, separate from whatever authoring-path rule is under dispute in the design doc you're investigating.
- `.docs/memory/projectState.md:42` — logs `ShoppableImage` explicitly as "Experience Builder component + standard content type," i.e. project memory already flags it as the dual-path exception.
- `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:26-33` (content-ownership table) and open item §10.2 (`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:131`, mirrored in `.docs/temp/openItems.md:53`) — record that whether PLP/PDP editorial blocks are Contentful-driven at all, and whether category landing pages are "SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences," are **still open/unconfirmed** with the client. `.docs/prd/homepage.md:62` records an unresolved requirement (HPC-010, "Reusable page builder templates") with a live client challenge — *"is this required? ... The ability to reuse an existing template is needed ... Is this possible within Studio?"* — showing that at the requirements level there is genuine, still-open ambiguity about how much page composition should move into Contentful Studio Experiences, which is the closest thing in the repo to direct support for the SA's underlying concern (though it's an open PRD question, not evidence about what's actually built).
- No test suite exists for either path (`overrides/app/components/contentful/**` and `experiences/**` have zero `.test`/`.spec` files), so there's no test-level evidence either way.

## Summary

The current codebase evidence leans toward **"keep the two paths separate"** for the components that actually exist and run today: `CollectionHero` and `ImageText` are clean, self-contained Experience Builder components with zero code overlap with the coded side, the four coded components (`HeroBanner`, `DuplexSection`, `VideoEmbed`, `ProductHero`) are consumed only from the Home page's `useContentful`-driven path and never touch `experiences/`, and the project's own documentation (`scripts/contentful/README.md`'s "Don't cross the streams," `.docs/architecture.md:187`, `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md:294`) already states the split as intended architecture, with dedicated tooling (autogenerated `definitions.ts`, a separate `sync:contentful` script) and even separate file-ownership rules enforcing it. The one genuine counter-example is `ShoppableImage`, which is real, concrete, code-level evidence that the SA's concern isn't purely hypothetical — it was deliberately scaffolded for dual use (Experience Builder registration *and* a standalone CDA content type/TS type), but it is a partial, currently-broken exception rather than a working precedent: the coded consumption path for it is entirely unbuilt (no page fetches it via `useContentful`), and where the two registrations do overlap (the `hotspots` field shape, and the `entryId`/`locale`/live-preview props), they are presently prop-incompatible. So the evidence is not fully one-sided: it supports keeping a hard separation as the default, while showing that the one place the team already tried to share a component across both paths ended up half-finished and inconsistent — which arguably strengthens rather than weakens the case for an explicit rule, since it shows what happens without one, but it does not support the SA's stronger claim that "most" components will end up dual-path, since 2 of 3 registered Experience components and all 4 coded components show no such overlap at all.

Neither of the two purely Experience-only components (`CollectionHero`, `ImageText`) accepts or uses `entryId`/`locale`/`ContentfulLivePreview` at all. So `ShoppableImage`'s `entryId`/`locale`/live-preview code is dead weight in its one currently-active registration path (Experience Builder) and only makes sense for the coded path it isn't actually wired into.
- Corroborating project memory: `.docs/memory/projectState.md:42` explicitly logs this as **"ShoppableImage component — Experience Builder component + standard content type"** with the content type "synced to Contentful (mock space) 2026-05-11" — i.e. the dual-registration is a known, deliberate (if unfinished) design, not an accident, but it has not been fully realized/tested for the coded side.

**Conclusion for item 3**: it is one implementation, deliberately scaffolded for both paths (registered in `definitions.ts` for Experience Builder, and separately schema-synced as a CDA content type), but currently only actually *consumed* through the Experience Builder path in running code, and its two registrations disagree on the `hotspots` prop shape — a concrete "owner call needed" situation, exactly as the design doc flags.

## 4. Git history

```
overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts:
  5aafaae 2026-07-13  fix(contentful): address CodeRabbit findings on codegen and docs
  d5012bc 2026-07-03  feat(contentful): Added Contentful Studio/Experiences definition codegen/automation
  cd60b7a 2026-06-12  Initial commit during Detailed Design phase

overrides/app/components/contentful/{heroBanner,duplexSection,videoEmbed,productHero}.tsx, index.ts:
  cd60b7a 2026-06-12  Initial commit during Detailed Design phase   (only commit for all five)

overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/shoppableImage.tsx:
  03524b5 2026-07-13, d5012bc 2026-07-03, cd60b7a 2026-06-12

scripts/contentful/content-types/shoppableImage.js:
  cd60b7a 2026-06-12  Initial commit during Detailed Design phase   (only commit; created same commit as shoppableImage.tsx)
```

All coded components and all three Experience components (plus the `shoppableImage.js` content-type schema) were introduced in the **same single initial commit** (`cd60b7a`, "Initial commit during Detailed Design phase") — there was no later, distinct commit where the project "decided" to split the two paths; both existed side by side from day one. `git show cd60b7a -s --format=fuller` shows no body text beyond the one-line subject, so no rationale is recorded there.

The two subsequent substantive commits (`d5012bc` "Added Contentful Studio/Experiences definition codegen/automation", `5aafaae` "fix(contentful): address CodeRabbit findings on codegen and docs") are about **tooling** (the `@cf`-tag → `definitions.ts` codegen pipeline) — not about the architectural split itself. The actual documented rationale for keeping the two paths distinct lives in project docs, not commit messages:
- `scripts/contentful/README.md:64-68` — section literally titled **"Don't cross the streams"**: *"A Studio Experiences component (`experiences/*.tsx`) does not belong in content-types/ — sync.js does not understand it. A content-type definition (content-types/*.js) does not belong in experiences/ — it is an API artefact, not a runtime component."*
- `.docs/architecture.md:187` — *"Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in .../experiences/definitions.ts and do not need a corresponding sync:contentful entry **unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio**."* (this is the explicit escape hatch that `shoppableImage` exercises)
- `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md:87-99` — `scripts/contentful/content-types/` is governed under a distinct "Owner: Integration / SI Partner" protection rule, separate from the (unprotected, autogenerated) `experiences/definitions.ts` — a further sign the two paths are intended to have different ownership/process, not just different code location.

## 5. `useContentful.ts` usage

`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` exports `useContentfulEntry` and `useContentfulEntries` (both plain CDA/CPA `fetch`-based hooks, lines 26-89 and 91-157). A repo-wide grep for importers of `useContentful` returns exactly one file: **`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`** (lines 24, 148, 175) — used in `HomeNormal` (`useContentfulEntries<HomepageEntry>('homepage')`, line 148) and `HomePreviewContent` (`useContentfulEntry<AnyContentfulEntry>(entryId, true)`, line 175).

It is **never** imported by `pages/experience/index.tsx` or by anything under `experiences/`. The Experience-Builder-rendered page instead uses the Contentful `contentful` JS SDK's `createClient` plus `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react`'s `useFetchBySlug`/`ExperienceRoot` (`pages/experience/index.tsx:4-5, 45-68`) — a completely separate data-fetching path from `useContentful.ts`. So today, `useContentful.ts` is used strictly outside the Experience-Builder-rendered page, confirming a clean split at the **data-fetching** layer, even though (per §3) the `ShoppableImage` component itself was coded with both consumption patterns in mind.

## 6. `.docs/` documentation of the authoring-model distinction

Documentation already describing this split (beyond the TSD in dispute) exists in several places:

- `scripts/contentful/README.md` — full write-up of "two different Contentful surfaces" (content types vs. Studio Experiences component definitions), ending in the explicit "Don't cross the streams" rule (lines 64-68, quoted above).
- `.docs/architecture.md:160-187` — "Contentful Content Type Management" section, culminating in the line noting Experience Builder components are "a separate concern," with the explicit caveat that a component *can* have both when "they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio" (line 187) — i.e., the doc anticipates and permits the exact `shoppableImage` situation.
- `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md:294` (§7.3, "Contentful schema as code") — *"Each definition pairs with a typed React component... Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module."* This is the current TSD's own architecture section stating the split as settled fact, separate from whatever authoring-path rule is under dispute in the design doc you're investigating.
- `.docs/memory/projectState.md:42` — logs `ShoppableImage` explicitly as "Experience Builder component + standard content type," i.e. project memory already flags it as the dual-path exception.
- `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:26-33` (content-ownership table) and open item §10.2 (`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:131`, mirrored in `.docs/temp/openItems.md:53`) — record that whether PLP/PDP editorial blocks are Contentful-driven at all, and whether category landing pages are "SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences," are **still open/unconfirmed** with the client. `.docs/prd/homepage.md:62` records an unresolved requirement (HPC-010, "Reusable page builder templates") with a live client challenge — *"is this required? ... The ability to reuse an existing template is needed ... Is this possible within Studio?"* — showing that at the requirements level there is genuine, still-open ambiguity about how much page composition should move into Contentful Studio Experiences, which is the closest thing in the repo to direct support for the SA's underlying concern (though it's an open PRD question, not evidence about what's actually built).
- No test suite exists for either path (`overrides/app/components/contentful/**` and `experiences/**` have zero `.test`/`.spec` files), so there's no test-level evidence either way.

## Summary

The current codebase evidence leans toward **"keep the two paths separate"** for the components that actually exist and run today: `CollectionHero` and `ImageText` are clean, self-contained Experience Builder components with zero code overlap with the coded side, the four coded components (`HeroBanner`, `DuplexSection`, `VideoEmbed`, `ProductHero`) are consumed only from the Home page's `useContentful`-driven path and never touch `experiences/`, and the project's own documentation (`scripts/contentful/README.md`'s "Don't cross the streams," `.docs/architecture.md:187`, `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md:294`) already states the split as intended architecture, with dedicated tooling (autogenerated `definitions.ts`, a separate `sync:contentful` script) and even separate file-ownership rules enforcing it. The one genuine counter-example is `ShoppableImage`, which is real, concrete, code-level evidence that the SA's concern isn't purely hypothetical — it was deliberately scaffolded for dual use (Experience Builder registration *and* a standalone CDA content type/TS type), but it is a partial, currently-broken exception rather than a working precedent: the coded consumption path for it is entirely unbuilt (no page fetches it via `useContentful`), and where the two registrations do overlap (the `hotspots` field shape, and the `entryId`/`locale`/live-preview props), they are presently prop-incompatible. So the evidence is not fully one-sided: it supports keeping a hard separation as the default, while showing that the one place the team already tried to share a component across both paths ended up half-finished and inconsistent — which arguably strengthens rather than weakens the case for an explicit rule, since it shows what happens without one, but it does not support the SA's stronger claim that "most" components will end up dual-path, since 2 of 3 registered Experience components and all 4 coded components show no such overlap at all.

content.text:
This is now thoroughly triangulated across all three sources. Here's the verdict.

## What each source shows

**Codebase (via Explore agent, full report above):**
- Only 3 components are registered as Studio Experience (`CollectionHero`, `ImageText`, `ShoppableImage`). The 4 coded components (`HeroBanner`, `DuplexSection`, `VideoEmbed`, `ProductHero`) are consumed only from the Home page's `useContentful`-driven path and never touch `experiences/`. Zero overlap for 6 of the 7 components that actually exist today.
- The one real exception, `ShoppableImage`, is registered for both paths but the two registrations are currently **prop-incompatible** (Studio's `hotspots` is a Text/string, the standalone content type's `hotspots` is an Object/array; `JSON.parse` on the array would throw and get silently swallowed). It's evidence the SA's concern isn't hypothetical, but it's a half-finished, currently-broken attempt, not a working precedent for "most things end up dual-path."
- The split is already established **independent of this TSD**: `scripts/contentful/README.md` states it explicitly under a section literally titled "Don't cross the streams," `.docs/architecture.md:187` and `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md:294` both describe it as settled architecture, and `scripts/contentful/content-types/` even has separate file-ownership rules from `experiences/definitions.ts`. The TSD's §5.5 rule isn't proposing something new, it's restating a decision the codebase already made and tooled for.

**Jira (full-project keyword search + specific tickets):**
- A project-wide search for "Experience Builder," "Studio Experience," or "drag-and-drop" across every SFCC ticket returns exactly **one hit**: SFCC-51 (the banner), and only in review comments, not the ticket's own description.
- SFCC-10 (Z.immerse) is the one epic that unambiguously calls for Studio-style, author-composed pages, and it's already correctly classified that way in the TSD's own §5.5 examples. No dispute there.
- SFCC-96 (mega menu) has Tim himself asking open questions about implementation options ("do we have any designs of what might be put in there... want to think about a few possible implementation options"), not asserting it should be Studio-placed. Genuinely undecided, not evidence for either side.
- SFCC-51 (banner) is the real, specific exception: Tim's comment 13363 states outright it'll be "a component in the Contentful Studio builder" with drag-and-drop placement, and his comment 13387 proposes (not yet accepted) an AC framing placement as "via Contentful Studio" with Category/Product ID targeting. This remains a **proposed**, not ratified, AC, no comment after it (14 Jul) confirms or rejects it. So even the one concrete counter-example is still unsettled at the ticket level.

**Confluence:** the PWA TSD (256835585) independently states "Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module", a third, independent corroboration of the same split, from a different document Tim himself isn't disputing.

## Verdict

Push back on the general claim, concede the specific exception.

Tim's broader assertion, "the components we build will most of the time being used in an experience builder", isn't supported by any of the three sources. Code shows the opposite (6 of 7 real components cleanly split), the ticket backlog shows the opposite (1 hit out of 20+ Contentful stories), and the split already exists as documented architecture outside this TSD, so removing §5.5's rule wouldn't remove the split, it would just make the TSD stop describing something that's still true and already enforced elsewhere.

But the banner (SFCC-51) is a real, evidenced exception, Tim has said twice, in his own words, on the ticket itself, that it should be Studio-placed with drag-and-drop and ID targeting. That AC is still proposed, not accepted, so the TSD shouldn't assert it either way yet, it should flag it as pending, matching what's actually true of the ticket.

## Recommended action

Keep §5.5's authoring-path rule and heuristic as-is (it's independently correct and already codebase-enforced), but reclassify the banner in Appendix C from its current implicit coded/Sprint-1 status to "authoring path pending SFCC-51's AC sign-off", since that's the one component where the real evidence says the current default classification may be wrong. Want me to draft that Appendix C edit and a reply to Tim's comment reflecting this?

content.thinking:
The user's making a solid point about context—for a handoff document meant to brief the incoming Contentful team, Tim's claim might actually hold water in a practical sense. By the time they take over, the Accenture developers will have already built out the coded components and synced the content-type schemas into Contentful, so from the new team's perspective, those content types would already exist as usable entities. rience Builder depends on whether that component is registered via `defineComponents` — the content type's mere existence in Contentful doesn't automatically make it composable in Studio's visual builder. So while incoming teams could theoretically browse and reference content entries across Contentful, only the components explicitly registered for Studio would be draggable/placeable in the Experience Builder UI. So there are really two separate systems in Contentful: content types (the schema and field definitions managed through the standard UI) and Experience Builder (the visual drag-and-drop canvas where authors compose pages using pre-registered frontend components that can optionally pull data from those content types).
