Good instinct to check, but the technical answer doesn't bear it out. Verified via the SDK's own type definitions and the repo's docs: **schema-syncing a content type and Studio-registering a component are two separate systems, and syncing does not put anything into Studio's canvas.**

## Why the "already in Contentful, so already in Studio" read doesn't hold technically

`npm run sync:contentful` only creates the content type in Contentful's Content Model section (fields, validations), the plain forms-based entry editor. Experience Builder's canvas only shows blocks that have gone through a separate, explicit `defineComponents` registration in `experiences/definitions.ts`. The SDK's own variable-type enum (`Text | RichText | Number | Date | Boolean | Location | Media | Object | Hyperlink | Array | Link`) has no "any content type" or generic reference-to-entry type that would let a synced content type show up as a draggable block automatically. The closest, `Link`, only lets a prop *inside an already-registered component* point at an arbitrary entry, it doesn't turn that entry's content type into an independent canvas block. And concretely, none of the 4 coded content sources (`heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero`) are reachable from the Experience-rendered page (`pages/experience/index.tsx`) at all, only the 3 things actually registered in `definitions.ts` are.

So by the time the Contentful team arrives, the coded/synced content types exist as ordinary Contentful entries, editable via standard forms, same as they are today. They don't become Studio Experience blocks just by existing. That would take someone explicitly registering them, the same `defineComponents` work Accenture devs do now.

## The softer version of your point, which is fair

If you mean something looser, once a specialized Contentful squad owns the space day-to-day, nothing stops them from later registering more components as Experience blocks themselves, that's true, it's just not automatic, and it's not something that's already happened by virtue of syncing. It would be new registration effort, done under their own ownership, after handover. That's consistent with Appendix A's Handoff Boundary, which already lists "register components in the experiences module" as Accenture's job during this engagement, not the incoming squad's default activity.

## Does this change the recommendation

Not the core one, the rule should stay, because it describes real, current, technically-enforced architecture, and the TSD's own stated job (§1.1) is to document what Accenture builds before handover, not to pre-design around what the next squad might optionally choose to do with their own effort later. But your question is worth one addition: a short forward-looking line, probably in Appendix A, noting the incoming squad may choose to register additional coded content types as Experience components post-handover, and that this is their call, not a build requirement here. That addresses Tim's instinct honestly without conceding a technical premise that doesn't hold up. Want me to draft that line, plus the reply to Tim covering both the verdict and this clarification?

Problem Statement\\n--------------------\\n\\n### 1.1 Context\\n\\nZimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards.\\n\\n### 1.2 Problem\\n\\nEditorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards.\\n\\n### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved\\n\\nWithout a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build.\\n\\n### 1.4 Success Criteria\\n\\n1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue.\\n2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories.\\n3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined.\\n4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners.\\n5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy.\\n\\n*These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.*\\n\\n---\\n\\n2. Options Analysis\\n-------------------\\n\\n> The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document.\\n\\n### 3.1 Options Summary\\n\\n| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync). + SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash). + Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. + The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages. - All SFCC-ID filtering happens once, in the MRT SSR layer; components hold none of their own. A bug there affects every page of that content type at once, with no fallback to catch it. | Yes (recommended) |\\n| **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift). - Couples the two systems. - Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected |\\n| **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash). - Ships unneeded entries to the browser. - Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No |\\n\\n### 3.2 Option Detail\\n\\n#### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering\\n\\nSFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means \\\"show on all pages of this type\\\". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5.\\n\\n#### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected)\\n\\nEditors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume.\\n\\n#### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)*\\n\\nDiscarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components.\\n\\n---\\n\\n4. Recommended Option & Rationale\\n---------------------------------\\n\\n### 4.1 Recommended Option\\n\\n**Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.**\\n\\n### 4.2 Rationale\\n\\nOption A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B introduces and requires a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238.\\n\\n### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted\\n\\n* Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages.\\n* This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5).\\n\\n---\\n\\n5. Technical Implementation\\n---------------------------\\n\\n### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow)\\n\\n1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X).\\n2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA).\\n3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type.\\n4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component.\\n5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output).\\n6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated).\\n7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys.\\n\\n> **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live.\\n\\n### 5.2 Component / API Changes\\n\\n| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New |\\n| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified |\\n| `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New |\\n| GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New |\\n\\n> Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**.\\n\\n### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces\\n\\n**Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields):\\n\\n| Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. |\\n| `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. |\\n| `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |\\n| `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |\\n\\n**Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert):\\n\\n`{\\nid: 'sfccCategoryId',\\nname: 'SFCC Category ID',\\ntype: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI\\nlocalized: false,\\nrequired: false,\\nvalidations: [],\\n}`\\n\\n**MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):**\\n\\n`const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({\\ncontent_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',\\nlocale: currentLocale,\\n});\\nconst matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => {\\nconst { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;\\n// null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render\\nreturn !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId;\\n});\\n// Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component\\nreturn matchedInserts;`\\n\\n**Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.\\n\\n**Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages.\\n\\n### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases\\n\\n| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error |\\n| Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case |\\n| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error |\\n| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case |\\n| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error |\\n| Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. Never in MRT or the browser bundle. |\\n| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). |\\n\\n**Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:\\n\\n* **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. Canonically Z.immerse (SFCC-10) and campaign/marketing landing pages, served via the `/:slug` route.\\n* **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.\\n* Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.\\n\\n---\\n\\n6. 1. Problem Statement
--------------------

### 1.1 Context

Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards.

### 1.2 Problem

Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards.

### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved

Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build.

### 1.4 Success Criteria

1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue.
2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories.
3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined.
4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners.
5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy.

*These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.*

---

2. Constraints & Assumptions
----------------------------

### 2.1 Constraints

| Constraint | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. |
| Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |
| Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). |
| Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions applied via npm run sync:contentful. Run manually by a developer today, not yet wired into CI (see Appendix B); never hand-created in the Contentful UI. |
| Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts (AU, US-domestic, US-international, UK, EU-domestic, EU-international, HK, ME), 9 Contentful locales, and 11 storefront-locale URL routes. Each storefront is backed by its own SFCC site; EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, which is why the route count (11) exceeds the SFCC-site count (8). The codebase wires 7 of the 8 SFCC sites today, with US-International (`ZimmermannUSIntl`) pending. No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and Section 7. |
| Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. |

### 2.2 Assumptions

| Assumption | Risk if Wrong |
| --- | --- |
| Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. |
| The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references; it validates against the live catalogue at authoring time, immediately showing the author when an entered ID has no match. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). |

This is a known, already-tracked item (`.docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md`), not new. Confirm the locale choice and rollout timing with the regional-config owner before Contentful's environment/locale bootstrap. See Section 7. |

---

3. Options Analysis
-------------------

> The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document.

### 3.1 Options Summary

| Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync). + SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash). + Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes. + The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages. - All SFCC-ID filtering happens once, in the MRT SSR layer; components hold none of their own. A bug there affects every page of that content type at once, with no fallback to catch it. | Yes (recommended) |
| **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift). - Couples the two systems. - Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected |
| **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash). - Ships unneeded entries to the browser. - Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No |

### 3.2 Option Detail

#### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5.

#### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected)

Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume.

#### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)*

Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components.

---

4. Recommended Option & Rationale
---------------------------------

### 4.1 Recommended Option

**Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.**

### 4.2 Rationale

Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B introduces and requires a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238.

### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted

* Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages.
* This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5).

---

5. Technical Implementation
---------------------------

### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow)

1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X).
2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA).
3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type.
4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component.
5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output).
6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated).
7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys.

> **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live.

### 5.2 Component / API Changes

| File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified |
| `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Not yet built. | New |
| GraphQL query layer | Introduce for composed pages that assemble multiple entries (target). | New |

> Reference-resolution (how an SFCC ID becomes rendered product/category data via a commerce hook) is deliberately not specified here. A working single-product bridge exists today (`productHero.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx` pass a Contentful `productId` into `useProduct`, client-side, against a mock space). Reconciling that bridge with the SSR-first and presentation-only rules is owned by **SFCC-238**.

### 5.3 Data Structures / Interfaces

**Content model - how SFCC IDs are stored** (non-localized structural fields):

| Field | Type | Localized | Applies To | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfccCategoryId` | ShortText | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | SFCC category ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all categories of that type. |
| `sfccProductId` | ShortText | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | SFCC master product ID this entry is scoped to. Null = show on all PDPs. |
| `sfccProductIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Campaign editorial, homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| `sfccCategoryIds` | ShortText (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

**Schema-as-code definition** (example, PLP Inline Grid Insert):

`{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol', // ShortText in the Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: [],
}`

**MRT SSR filter (PLP example, pseudocode):**

`const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({
content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',
locale: currentLocale,
});
const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter((entry) => {
const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;
// null = show on all categories; a specific ID = scoped render
return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId;
});
// Only matched entries are passed to the presentation-only component
return matchedInserts;`

**Component contract:** the component receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer; it holds no SFCC ID comparison logic; it renders all entries it receives, in order; an empty array renders nothing. This keeps components presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.

**Cache-key requirement:** any page whose SSR output depends on `sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId` filtering must include that ID in its MRT cache key (PLP: locale + categoryId [+ page]; PDP: locale + productId; homepage: locale only). Omitting the ID causes editorial content to appear on the wrong pages.

### 5.4 Error Handling & Edge Cases

| Scenario | Expected Behaviour | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Serve stale SSR cache within the SWR window; fall back to a bare page render if the cache is cold. Never block page render on CMS availability. **Open:** footer and homepage have no editorial-free fallback, so a cold-cache bare render is visually broken during a full outage; hard-dependency versus last-known-good fallback is pending Tim (Section 7). | Error |
| Contentful entry field null or missing | Null-safe render: omit CTA/image if absent; no uncaught exceptions; log a warning (authoring issue, not a system failure). | Edge case |
| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately; do not process the payload; log origin, timestamp, truncated signature. | Error |
| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero and blocks deploy; developer runs `npm run migrate:contentful` and re-triggers. | Edge case |
| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically; review partial state and write a compensating migration; coordinate with content editors before re-running. | Error |
| Preview (CPA) content requested in the browser | Supported by design on non-production tiers only. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK requires the CPA token in the browser for real-time updates; the `/preview` and `?preview` routes return an explicit non-indexable error when the token is absent, and the token is provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat, never on staging/production (see 5.5 and PR #43). | Edge case |
| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load (affects Vimeo embeds in editorial). Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley (SFCC-106). | Edge case |

> **Connection-pool isolation:** blast-radius containment for SSR upstreams is defined in **PWA TSD (256835585) 12.1**, not restated here. Each storefront has its own SFCC site (8 at target; 7 wired today, US-International pending); EU-domestic's single site serves 4 language routes, giving 11 storefront-locale routes in total (10 wired today). Full environment, alias, and locale setup is maintained in the Contentful CMS - Setup & Operations runbook (318472193). See the REG-005 item in Section 7.

| Surface | Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in the bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | Browser on non-prod tiers only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (real-time updates over postMessage). Provisioned only on dev/test/sit/uat; preview routes 404 and `noindex` when absent. There is no MRT preview proxy. See 02-contentful.md 9 and PR #43. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI service account, and each developer's own local `.env` | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Personal per-developer tokens for local work; a separate CI service-account token for automation. Never in MRT or the browser bundle. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish (target; receiver not yet built). |

**Authoring-path rule - Studio Experiences versus coded content-type components.** Two authoring/render paths exist and each new content type must be assigned to one:

* **Studio Experience** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`, registered via `defineComponents`; definitions produced by `npm run generate:contentful`): use when the content is a **whole, author-composed page that owns its own URL**, arranged visually in Contentful Studio and published without a deploy. * **Coded content-type component** (`overrides/app/components/contentful/`, a CDA content type + typed component consumed via `useContentful`): use when the content is a **fixed slot in a dev-built commerce template** where the author only edits field values. Canonically homepage modules, PLP inserts/bottom zone, PDP slide-out tabs, footer, navigation, announcement banner, size guide.
* **Heuristic:** does the author decide placement and neighbours? Studio Experience. Does the dev fix placement and the author only fill fields? Coded component.
* Build the coded version by default; only also register a Studio block when the content must appear inside an author-composed page. Riders: `shoppableImage` straddles both (owner call needed); avoid building the same concept twice.

## Checking the claim against what's actually planned

Appendix C lists 17 identified content types across Sprint 1, Sprint 2, and Sprint TBD. Sorting them by which authoring path they actually fit:

That's 1 confirmed, 1 conceded, 2 ambiguous, and 10 with no support at all. Nowhere near "most of the time."

## A harder problem than the count: architecture rules some of these out entirely

Sprint 2's four items (Size Guide, PLP Bottom Zone, PLP Inline Grid Insert, PDP Accordion), the largest concrete near-term batch, aren't just unlikely to be Studio-based, they **can't be**, given how Studio Experience actually works. Confirmed earlier: Experience-rendered pages are fetched by `useFetchBySlug` as whole, standalone, author-composed pages on their own `/:slug` route. There's no mechanism in Studio for "inject this block into SFCC's own PLP template only when the category ID matches", that's exactly what Option A's SSR-side ID filtering was designed to solve, and it's a coded-content-type mechanism by construction. So the biggest specific batch of upcoming work is architecturally locked to the coded path regardless of preference, not by convention, by what each system is actually capable of.

It would mean Studio ends up the busier of the two paths, which is a claim about volume, not about whether each new content type still needs correctly sorting into one path or the other. The rule's job is to answer "which path does this one belong to", that job doesn't go away just because one answer turns out to be more common. If anything, more volume on one side is an argument for keeping the sorting rule clear, not dropping it.

## Verdict

Not a valid reason to drop the split, for two independent reasons: empirically, only a small minority of the actual planned backlog is Studio-bound (and the largest near-term batch is technically barred from it), and logically, even the most generous version of the claim (Studio ends up busier long-term) doesn't argue against having a rule to sort things, it argues for one. content.text:
Take one real example from Sprint 2: **PLP Inline Grid Insert** (SFCC-190, uses `sfccCategoryId`), a Contentful-authored tile that shows up inside the product grid on a category page.

## As a coded component (what's actually planned)

A shopper hits `/womens/dresses`, that's the real PWA Kit PLP page devs already built, showing live SFCC inventory: products, pagination, filters, sorting. The MRT SSR layer separately fetches all `plpInlineGridInsert` entries from Contentful, keeps only the ones whose `sfccCategoryId` is null or matches "dresses," and hands those to a component that slots into the existing grid at a fixed position. The page, the product data, the grid layout, all of that is devs' code. Contentful only supplies "what goes in this one tile."

Shelf analogy: **we built the shelf (the PLP page), Contentful just decides what item sits on it.**

## What it would take for this to be a Studio Experience component instead

For an author to drag this onto a page in Contentful Studio, it has to live on a page that Contentful itself owns end to end, fetched by its own slug, like `/immerse/summer-campaign`. That page doesn't touch SFCC's product catalogue at all, everything on it comes from Contentful.

Now ask: could Studio instead reach into `/womens/dresses`, the real PLP page, and drop a tile into its live, paginated, SFCC-driven grid at the right spot? No, there's no mechanism for that. Studio doesn't know that page exists, it can only compose whole pages that live entirely inside Contentful. To make the grid insert "Studio-based," you'd either have to rebuild the entire PLP, live product data, pagination, filtering and all, inside Contentful (not realistic, that data has to come from SFCC), or invent some new system for Studio to inject into someone else's page, which doesn't exist today and isn't what anyone's asked for.

Shelf analogy again: **you can't drag a shelf item onto a wall in a different house. The shelf only exists in the house we built.**

## Contrast: why Z.immerse actually works as Studio

`/immerse/summer-campaign` isn't injected into anything, it's a whole standalone page, no SFCC PLP or PDP involved. Studio builds the whole room, not just what's on a shelf inside a room someone else built. That's the structural difference that makes Z.immerse a genuine Studio case and PLP Inline Grid Insert not one.

## Why this matters for "most of the time"

It's not just that the odds are low, three of Sprint 2's four items (PLP Bottom Zone, PLP Inline Grid Insert, PDP Accordion) work exactly like the grid insert, tiles injected into pages devs already built. There's no version of Studio, as it exists today, that can do that job. So for the biggest specific batch of near-term work, it's not "unlikely to end up in Studio," it's "structurally can't."

The component is a simple React component that renders a button with some text. ```ts // src/components/Button.tsx import React from 'react'; interface ButtonComponentProps { text: string; } export const Button: React.FC = ({ text, ...experienceProps }) => { return ; }; ``` To learn more about creating custom components for your experience, check out the [register custom components guide](/experiences/register-custom-components). ### Register your component Next, your component needs to be registered with the Experiences SDK. This is done with the help of the `defineComponents` function which can be imported from the `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` package. We suggest registering your components once at the startup of your application; for example in the **index.tsx** (or like) file. ```ts // src/registeredComponents.ts import { defineComponents } from '@contentful/experiences-sdk-react'; import { Button } from './components/Button'; defineComponents([ { component: Button, definition: { id: 'button', name: 'Button', category: 'Custom Components', variables: { text: { displayName: 'Text', type: 'Text', defaultValue: 'Click me!', }, }, }, }, ]); ``` Above, we register the `Button` component and provide a component definition that Experiences use to help you configure the component in the editor. In the component definition, we specify the `id` and `name` of the component, the `category` (where it is displayed in the Components tab), and the `variables` it supports. We configure the `text` variable to be of type `Text` and provide a default value. This variable is editable in the Experiences and its value is passed down to the `Button` component as a prop. To learn more about the component definitions and what features they provide, please refer to the [Component definition schema](/experiences/component-definition-schema). ### Create a Contentful client To fetch the experience, create a Contentful client. The client requires a few initialization variables. In our example, we pull these variables from environment variables. See documentation for the specific framework you use to learn how to use environment variables within it. We recommend creating the client once in your application and reusing it across the components that need to access Experiences. For more info on using the JavaScript library for [CDA](/references/content-delivery-api/overview) and [CPA](/references/content-preview-api/overview) and how get access to the variables needed, refer to [Getting Started with Contentful and JavaScript](/sdks/javascript/tutorials/using-js-cda-sdk). ```ts // src/contentfulClient.ts import { createClient } from 'contentful'; export const client = createClient({ // your space id space: import.meta.env.VITE_CTFL_SPACE_ID, // your environment id environment: import.meta.env.VITE_CTFL_ENV_ID, // Supported values: 'preview.contentful.com' or 'cdn.contentful.com', host: import.meta.env.VITE_CTFL_API_HOST, // needs to be access token if host = 'cdn.contentful.com' and preview token if 'preview.contentful.com' accessToken: import.meta.env.VITE_CTFL_TOKEN }); ``` ### Display the experience The Experiences SDK uses the Contentful client to fetch the experience. The Experiences SDK includes helpful hooks, such as `useFetchBySlug`, which allows you to fetch an experience by its slug (configured in the settings tab for the experience) or the `useFetchById`, which fetches the experience by its ID. The `experienceTypeId` is the ID of the content model set up for experiences. To get the ID, log in to the Contentful web app, open the specific content model and click **Copy ID**. ![The Copy ID button for Experiences](file:docs/assets/images/copy-id-button.png) The hooks return the experience object, which can be rendered using the `ExperienceRoot` component. The `ExperienceRoot` component defines where the experience controls the content that is rendered. With `ExperienceRoot`, you have the flexibility to either allow your team to build entire pages or limit them to modifying specific sections of a webpage. Read both carefully against the claims we've made. Verdict: **largely supported, strongly on some points, but one part of the earlier reasoning needs a correction.**

## Where the Studio docs support our position

**The heuristic isn't an internal invention, it's Contentful's own persona model.** The docs define four roles: Developer (builds components, registers them), Marketer (assembles layouts from those components), Editor (fills in content), Designer. That Developer/Marketer split is exactly what our heuristic asks: "does the author decide placement and neighbours" (Marketer persona, by Contentful's own definition) versus "does the dev fix placement and the author only fills fields" (Editor persona, filling entries whose layout someone else already built). This is a stronger form of the argument than what we had before, we're not just matching an internal convention, we're matching Contentful's own documented product model.

**"Syncing a content type doesn't make it Studio-usable" is now vendor-confirmed, not just codebase-inferred.** The doc states: *"During setup, a dedicated 'Experiences' content type is generated per space."* An Experience is its own distinct content-type kind, auto-generated by Contentful specifically for Experiences, separate from the hand-defined content types devs sync via schema-as-code (`shoppableImage`, `homepage`, etc.). That's a data-model-level separation, not just a tooling convention someone in this project chose. Nothing about running `sync:contentful` touches or creates that special Experience content type.

**The codebase's implementation is a direct match to Contentful's own reference pattern**, not a project-specific interpretation. The doc's example code registers components with `defineComponents([{ component, definition: { id, name, variables: { type: 'Text', ... } } }])` and fetches with `useFetchBySlug` + `ExperienceRoot`, that's the exact shape found in `definitions.ts` and `pages/experience/index.tsx`. Good confirmation the codebase is following the vendor's intended architecture, not an ad hoc pattern.

## The one correction

One line changes something I stated too strongly earlier: *"With `ExperienceRoot`, you have the flexibility to either allow your team to build entire pages or limit them to modifying specific sections of a webpage."*

I'd claimed Studio "literally cannot" touch part of an existing SFCC-rendered page, only whole standalone pages. That's overstated. `ExperienceRoot` can technically be mounted inside just one section of a larger page, a dev could embed it at a fixed spot inside the PLP template.

But here's why that doesn't actually change the recommendation: doing that would mean fetching one specific experience by a **fixed slug** at that mount point, e.g., a dev pre-wiring "on the dresses PLP, render the experience named `plp-dresses-insert` at this spot." That requires a manually authored, manually mapped experience-slug for every single category or product that needs an insert, exactly the kind of hand-maintained mapping between SFCC and Contentful that Option B (mirroring the catalogue) was already rejected for. The dynamic behavior Option A actually needs, "any entry tagged with this category ID shows up automatically, no per-page authoring required", isn't what section-scoped `ExperienceRoot` gives you. So the corrected claim is: Studio *can* touch a page section, but doing so for Sprint 2's needs would reintroduce the exact manual-mapping problem this TSD's design was chosen to avoid, not that it's mechanically impossible.

## On the SFCC Connector doc

Separate from the authoring-path question, but worth flagging: it describes a **pick-from-a-list-and-click** UI (search products/categories, select, embed), not a type-an-ID-then-validate flow. Our §2.2 assumption text ("validates against the live catalogue... immediately showing the author when an entered ID has no match") and Jhoan's Jira comment ("if the author types in a wrong product/category, it won't show anything") both describe a type-then-validate mechanic that doesn't match the actual product. Worth a small correction there, unrelated to today's question but a real one.

## Bottom line

The claim, both the rebuttal to Tim and the heuristic, is supported, and now on firmer footing than before since it lines up with Contentful's own documented model, not just what's in this codebase. The one thing to fix is dropping "technically impossible" in favor of the more precise "possible, but only by reintroducing the manual mapping problem Option A exists to avoid."
